To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high doses of chemotherapy with prophylactic antibiotic coverage are not superior to standard chemotherapy in patients with advanced breast cancer.
high doses of FAC chemotherapy in protected environment do not improve response rates, time to progression and survival compared with standard FAC chemotherapy.

high-dose induction chemotherapy in protected environment is not superior to standard dose chemotherapy in terms of overall response rate, complete remission rate, time to progression and survival in patients with metastases of breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of high-dose combination chemotherapy and the protective value of a protected environment in the treatment of metastatic breast disease.
the evaluation of the efficacy and safety of high-dose induction chemotherapy in patients with disseminated breast cancer.
the use of high-dose combination chemotherapy with prophylactic antibiotic coverage in a protected environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this trial did not prove or disprove the efficacy of high doses of chemotherapy, or the protective value of a protected environment in metastatic breast carcinoma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high-dose chemotherapy is not superior to standard-dose chemotherapy, and that the protected environment is not superior to a conventional hospital room.

the use of high doses of chemotherapy, in protected environments, with prophylactic antibiotic administration, does not result in higher objective response rates, longer times to progression, or improved survival in patients with metastases breast cancer.

high-dose induction chemotherapy in combination with prophylactic measures against infection in protected environments does not offer any advantage over standard-dose chemotherapy in the management of metastatic breast carcinoma.
